author: dusan-nikolic
description: Looted during the Revolution, the cathedral of Paris was falling into ruin and there was talk of razing it. In 1831, a young writer published a novel that changed its fate.

hero.hook: Before it became the symbol of French Gothic, Notre-Dame was a ruin that Paris was thinking of tearing down.

blocks.text: Construction of Notre-Dame de Paris began in **1163**. It is one of the first churches built in the [[Gothic style]]. Bishop [[Maurice de Sully]] started the project, and King **Louis VII** financed it. Both their portraits appear on a tympanum, the sculpted surface above the south-west entrance.

The cathedral stands on the [[Île de la Cité]], a natural island in the Seine and the political and religious heart of Paris and France through the centuries. The bishop's seat, it faced the royal palace. The bulk of the building was finished by the end of the 13th century, the exterior by the mid-14th. Then came neglect. Centuries later, it would be saved by a young writer in love with Gothic architecture, and by his novel.

After four centuries, Notre-Dame suffered heavy losses during the French Revolution. Religious worship was banned in Paris in **1793**: the cathedral was looted and vandalized. The [[gallery of kings]], a row of statues of Old Testament kings on the main facade, was singled out. The revolutionaries took the sculptures down and beheaded every "king." Most of the bells were melted down.

blocks.caption: The heads of the kings of Judah, cut off in 1793 and now kept at the Musée de Cluny.

blocks.text: Within a few years, the building changed function several times. It served as a warehouse, then became a [[Temple of Reason]], the name given to buildings that celebrated the values of the Revolution. The church reopened in **1802**. Two years later, it hosted the imperial coronation of **Napoleon Bonaparte**. The cathedral of Paris was nonetheless in a sorry state.

After decades of neglect and vandalism, Notre-Dame was decrepit. The Paris authorities seriously discussed razing it. A young writer and poet, [[Victor Hugo]], would have none of it. In **1831**, he published his novel *Notre-Dame de Paris*, the fruit of **three years** of intense study of the building and a lifelong passion for Gothic architecture.

blocks.caption: Notre-Dame de Paris, the novel by Victor Hugo published in 1831.

blocks.text: The writer wanted to preserve a monument he saw as being of national importance. His passionate, vivid descriptions of the cathedral gripped French readers. They conjured up the image of a collective work, built by French people of every rank. The intellectual elite of Paris raised its voice. On May 31, **1842**, Hugo and other poets, artists and thinkers signed a petition to restore the church.

sections.title: Victor Hugo takes up his pen

blocks.text: Thanks to Hugo, readers now saw Notre-Dame as the symbol of every Gothic monument in France. King **Louis Philippe** announced the restoration of Gothic buildings across the country. Notre-Dame's was entrusted to the architects [[Viollet-le-Duc]] and Jean-Baptiste Lassus. Work officially began in **1845**.
Most of the restoration of Notre-Dame is credited to Viollet-le-Duc: Lassus died in 1857, long before the work was finished.

Over two decades, the two architects completely restored the interior. Outside, they fitted the gallery of kings with new statues, rebuilt the spire, replaced damaged stones, restored the portals and added **100 statues** to the facade. In **1864**, the work was officially complete. Viollet-le-Duc's interpretation stirred controversy: had he restored the cathedral as it really was? No matter, Notre-Dame was saved.

The iconic status won in the 19th century has been confirmed in our own time. On April 15, **2019**, the cathedral caught fire. The whole world watched the partly wooden roof and the spire of the Parisian landmark collapse. This time, the devastated church did not need another novel. Victor Hugo's message still resonated, nearly two centuries later.

blocks.caption: April 15, 2019: Viollet-le-Duc's spire collapses in the fire.

blocks.text: Notre-Dame is recognized everywhere as the archetypal Gothic church. The world answered the call and funded its reconstruction with nearly **one billion dollars**. The cathedral escaped destruction once again, and united the planet along the way. It reopened to visitors on December 7, **2024**, with restoration work still under way.

blocks.text: Looted during the Revolution and slated for demolition, Notre-Dame owes its survival to Victor Hugo's novel, which turned a ruin into the symbol of French Gothic that the whole world wanted to save in 2019.
